agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager would read this as a standard teacher-to-trainer letter: it admits the GMP gap, never shows the signed, state-audited training records, and so gives her little reason to make the phone call.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim and invents no numbers, though phrases like 'training that sticks' and 'expect to learn both quickly' stretch a little past the evidence.

works_the_facts.reason: It gives the raw figures but never puts them in their strongest form: the 20-to-12-hour redesign (a 40% cut, which is the honest replacement for the half-time claim) is left out, and so is the 17-point (about 41% relative) rise in the AP pass rate.

right_comparison.reason: The 12-hour teacher training appears without the 20-hour program it replaced, so the reader sees no before-and-after and no proof the writer has already shortened onboarding.

qualification.reason: The GMP gap is hedged with a vague 'expect to learn quickly' when there was a checkable fact to use (the GMP course finishing May 2), and the June 14 earliest start date, which the reader needs, is left out.

objections.reason: The letter raises the reader's main doubt, no regulated-plant experience, and leaves it unanswered, even though the signed training records, the two clean state audits and the GMP course in progress would have met it directly.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter as requested, but it is still full of placeholders even though the name, company, plant and HR manager (Karen Doyle) were all known.
